{{ElectionsAK}}
The '''2026 United States Senate election in Alaska''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Alaska]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Dan Sullivan (U.S. senator)|Dan S. Sullivan]] is seeking a third term. He is being challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former congresswoman [[Mary Peltola]]. The election will be conducted under [[Instant-runoff voting|ranked-choice voting]].

A [[nonpartisan primary]] election was held on August 18 to determine the four candidates in the general election. Peltola and Sullivan were the first to advance with 49.5% and 41.4% of the vote respectively, followed by Republican former U.S. Forest Service employee Daniel J. Sullivan and Republican perennial candidate Gerald Heikes.

Democrats have not won a Senate election in Alaska since [[2008 United States Senate election in Alaska|2008]].

==Primary election==
Under Alaska's voting system, all candidates, regardless of party, run on the same primary ballot. The top four candidates in the primary advance to the general election, which is then conducted using [[ranked-choice voting]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Top-four primary |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Top-four_primary |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=19 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Background ===
Incumbent Republican [[Dan Sullivan (U.S. senator)|Dan Sullivan]] announced his run for re-election in early 2025. He was first elected in [[2014 United States Senate election in Alaska|2014]], defeating [[Mark Begich]], the most recent Democrat to represent Alaska in the [[U.S. Senate]]. He was last re-elected in [[2020 United States Senate election in Alaska|2020]], prior to the implementation of Alaska's ranked-choice voting system.<ref name=":0" /> Facing few obvious swing state targets to regain the Senate majority in [[2026 United States Senate elections|2026]], Democrats began looking towards more Republican-leaning states, such as [[2026 United States Senate special election in Ohio|Ohio]] and [[2026 United States Senate election in Texas|Texas]], as potential targets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Neukam |first=Stephen |date=2025-08-06 |title=Senate Democrats' top remaining targets for the 2026 midterms |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/08/06/senate-democrats-2026-elections-candidates |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref> Among these states was Alaska, where Senate Democratic leader [[Chuck Schumer]] heavily courted former U.S. Representative [[Mary Peltola]], the last Democrat to win any statewide election in Alaska, to run for Senate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nichols |first=Hans |last2=Neukam |first2=Stephen |date=2025-08-13 |title=Scoop: Schumer courts Peltola for Alaska Senate race |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/08/13/alaska-senate-peltola-schumer-sullivan |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref> Peltola narrowly lost her congressional seat in 2024, and had considered running for either Senate or [[2026 Alaska gubernatorial election|governor]], but she ultimately decided to enter the Senate race in early 2026, setting up the race between her and Sullivan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Herz |first=Nathaniel |date=2025-07-15 |title=Dems are 'salivating' over a Peltola bid for Senate, but Alaska governor race could be ‘wide open’ |url=https://alaskabeacon.com/2025/07/15/dems-are-salivating-over-a-peltola-bid-for-senate-but-alaska-governor-race-could-be-wide-open/ |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Alaska Beacon |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thiessen |first=Mark |date=2026-01-12 |title=Democrat Mary Peltola, barrier-breaking ex-Alaska congresswoman, is challenging Republican Dan Sullivan in Senate race |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrat-mary-peltola-barrier-breaking-ex-alaska-congresswoman-is-challenging-republican-dan-sullivan-in-senate-race |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=PBS News |language=en-us}}</ref>

====Daniel James Sullivan====
'''Daniel James Sullivan Jr.''' (born June 1957)<ref name=Bohrer2026a>{{Cite web |last=Bohrer |first=Becky |date=2026-06-09 |title=The other Dan Sullivan in Alaska’s US Senate race says candidacy was ‘my choice,’ not a sham |url=https://apnews.com/article/alaska-senate-dan-sullivan-peltola-68ca38749253c6bf52d13051fda01251 |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=AP News |language=en|quote=}}</ref> is a retired teacher and [[United States Forest Service]] employee from [[Petersburg, Alaska]], who filed to run as a Republican three days before the filing deadline.<ref name=SullivanPressRelease>{{Cite press release |title=Dan Sullivan Challenges Dan Sullivan for U.S. Senate Seat: Urges Alaskans to defeat incumbent, elect a Sullivan who Stands up for Alaska |date=2026-05-29 |publisher=Sullivan for Senate |url=https://www.sullivanforsenate.com/press |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260529204149/https://www.sullivanforsenate.com/press |archive-date=2026-05-29}}</ref> In an interview with the ''[[Petersburg Pilot]]'', Sullivan stated that he had been considering running against the incumbent U.S. Senator for 12 years, and remarked that he finally decided to run after the Senator's lack of opposition to the [[Anti-Weaponization Fund]].<ref name=Morrow2026a /> Senator Sullivan said this was "an effort to confuse Alaskans" and "dirty politics" by Democrats, calling Dan J. Sullivan a "sham candidate".  This was denied by Dan J. Sullivan, who called himself a "pragmatic Republican centrist". It was also denied by Mary Peltola's campaign, the Alaska Democratic Party, and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Senator Sullivan threatened legal action if the [[Lieutenant Governor of Alaska]] did not remove Dan J. Sullivan from the ballot.<ref name="cnn dan sullivan">{{Cite web |last1=Raju |first1=Ranu |last2=Fayez |first2=Aleena |date=2026-06-07 |title=GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan is raising alarms about an eleventh-hour challenger: Dan J. Sullivan |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/07/politics/dan-sullivan-alaska-senate-ballot |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=CNN |language=en-us}}</ref>

Dan J. Sullivan grew up in the [[Chicago metropolitan area]], and has lived in [[Southeast Alaska]] since 1980. He worked for the [[United States Forest Service]] in his early career before beginning a career as an elementary school teacher.<ref name=Bohrer2026a /> Sullivan taught in elementary schools for over 20 years before retiring.<ref name=Heckart2026a>{{Cite web |last=Heckart |first=Taylor |date=2026-06-04 |title=It’s no joke: A second Dan Sullivan says he really does want to be Alaska’s next senator |url=https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-06-04/its-no-joke-a-second-dan-sullivan-says-he-really-does-want-to-be-alaskas-next-senator |access-date=2026-06-27 |work=Alaska Public Media}}</ref> He was appointed to the city of Petersburg's Public Safety Advisory Board in December 2021.<ref name=Heckart2026a /> He served in that position until October 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dan Sullivan |url=https://www.petersburgak.gov/directory-listing/dan-sullivan |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=Petersburg, Alaska |language=en}}</ref> He stated that he was a member of the [[Alaskan Independence Party]] from when he moved to Alaska in 1980 until the party's dissolution in late 2025.<ref name=Heckart2026a /><ref name=Morrow2026a>{{Cite web |last=Morrow |first=Caleb |date=2026-06-04 |title=Petersburg's Dan Sullivan challenges Senator Dan Sullivan |url=HTTPS://www.petersburgpilot.com/story/2026/06/04/news/petersburgs-dan-sullivan-challenges-senator-dan-sullivan/15854.html |access-date=2026-06-27 |work=Petersburg Pilot}}</ref> 

Sullivan's initial campaign announcement stated that he was "focused on unseating the incumbent, putting Alaska first, and restoring accountability, common sense, and public service to Washington, D.C."<ref name=SullivanPressRelease /> He later described his political philosophy as "a pragmatic Republican centrist" similar to [[Lisa Murkowski]], with influence from [[Rand Paul]].<ref name=Bohrer2026a /> Incumbent U.S. Senator Daniel Scott Sullivan argued in an early June 2026 interview with [[CNN]] that "[Daniel James Sullivan's] whole purpose of running is to confuse Alaskans, to make him, make them think – Alaskan voters – that somehow he’s me, so they could rig the vote in favor of [[Mary Peltola]]."<ref name="cnn dan sullivan"/> An analysis of [[Federal Election Commission]] records by [[KTUU-TV]] showed that he had donated to Peltola's previous campaigns, including $100 in 2022 and $30 in 2024. KTUU reported that "That financial history is the extent of the documented link between the Petersburg Sullivan and the Peltola campaign."<ref name=CourtneySimon2026>{{Cite web |last1=Courtney |first1=Wil |last2=Simon |first2=Matthew |date=2026-06-13 |title=Two Dan Sullivans: Petersburg candidate poised for removal from ballot by state |url=https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/13/two-dan-sullivans-petersburg-candidate-poised-removal-ballot-by-state/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |work=KTUU-TV}}</ref> His initial press release and website design were supported by political strategist Amber Lee, who has previously worked with Democratic campaigns in Alaska.<ref name=Courtney2026a>{{Cite web |last=Courtney |first=Wil |date=2026-06-04 |title=Sullivan vs. Sullivan: Senator accuses Peltola of ‘rigging’ election — but evidence of her involvement is unclear |url=https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/04/sullivan-vs-sullivan-senator-accuses-peltola-rigging-election-evidence-her-involvement-is-unclear/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |work=KTUU-TV}}</ref> Lee has publicly spoken in favor of Peltola's candidacy, including in a January 2026 interview with [[The Hill (newspaper)|''The Hill'']].<ref name=Courtney2026a /><ref name=ElissaSlotkin>{{Cite web |last=Mueller |first=Julia |date=2026-01-15 |title=Peltola’s entrance in Alaska Senate race gives Democrats hope |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5689076-alaska-senate-race-democrats/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |work=The Hill}}</ref>

''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reported that weeks before the election, polls showed that approximately one third of voters likely to vote in the primary election could not distinguish the two candidates.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Epstein |first=Reid J. |date=2014-08-13 |title=Alaska Election Offers Two Chances to Vote for Dan Sullivan |url=http://online.wsj.com/articles/alaska-election-offers-two-chances-to-vote-for-dan-sullivan-1407897002 |access-date=2026-06-27 |work=Wall Street Journal |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Dan J. Sullivan's candidacy was the subject of legal debate, which {{As of|2026|6|27|df=US|lc=y}} is expected to advance to the [[Alaska Supreme Court]].<ref name=Ruskin2026a>{{Cite web |last=Ruskin |first=Liz |date=2026-06-27 |title=Judge puts 2nd Dan Sullivan back on ballot in Alaska’s U.S. Senate race |url=https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/2026-06-26/judge-puts-2nd-dan-sullivan-back-on-ballot-in-alaskas-u-s-senate-race |access-date=2026-06-27 |work=Alaska Public Media}}</ref> In its initial response to Sullivan's candidacy filing, the Alaska Division of Elections stated that Sullivan's name would appear on the ballot as "Sullivan, Dan J. (Registered Republican)."<ref name=Hanson2026a>{{Cite web |last=Hanson |first=Lars |date=2026-06-27 |title=Judge orders Petersburg’s Dan J. Sullivan onto Alaska U.S. Senate primary ballot |url=https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/06/27/judge-orders-petersburgs-dan-j-sullivan-onto-alaska-us-senate-primary-ballot/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |work=[[KTUU-TV]]}}</ref>

An Alaskan election official ordered Sullivan's name removed from the ballot, as his candidacy "was not filed in order to declare an actual good-faith candidacy for the office of United States Senator, but was instead filed with a purpose to confuse or mislead and to thereby compromise the ballot’s fairness or neutrality",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruskin |first=Liz |date=2026-06-15 |title=Alaska Elections Division makes it official, says Dan J. Sullivan can’t run against Sen. Dan S. Sullivan |url=https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/2026-06-15/alaska-elections-division-makes-it-official-says-dan-j-sullivan-cant-run-against-sen-dan-s-sullivan |access-date=2026-06-29 |work=Alaska Public Media}}</ref> a decision he appealed.<ref> https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5936869-dan-sullivan-ballot-challenge</ref> Anchorage Superior Court judge Thomas A. Matthews reversed the Division of Elections' decision to exclude Sullivan from the primary ballot on June 26. Matthews' decision ruled that the "good-faith" standard for ballot access was not supported by Alaska law, the Division of Elections' regulations, or [[Article One of the United States Constitution#Section 3: Senate|Article One, Section 3 of the United States Constitution]].<ref name=Hanson2026a /><ref name=Ruskin2026a /><ref name=DeMarban2026a>{{Cite web |last=DeMarban |first=Alex |date=2026-06-27 |title=Judge allows namesake challenger to Sen. Dan Sullivan to appear on Alaska ballot |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/06/26/superior-court-judge-rules-in-favor-of-namesake-challenger-to-sen-dan-sullivan/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |work=Anchorage Daily News}}</ref> On July 2nd the [[Alaska Supreme Court]] affirmed the decision, ordering Sullivan's name to be listed on the August 18th primary ballot.<ref name="adn supreme court">{{Cite web |last=DeMarban |first=Alex |title=Alaska Supreme Court allows namesake challenger to U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan to appear on the ballot |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/06/29/alaska-supreme-court-rules-that-dan-j-sullivan-can-appear-on-the-ballot-against-sen-dan-sullivan/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=Anchorage Daily News}}</ref> The Division of Elections released a sample ballot that will distinguish between the two Sullivans by listing Dan J. Sullivan as "Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr." and no party affiliation (despite Sullivan filing as a Republican) and identifying Dan S. Sullivan as the incumbent, which the DoE had not done for any other incumbent for at least 10 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/06/30/election-officials-sample-ballot-shows-how-they-seek-to-distinguish-two-dan-sullivans-in-us-senate-race/|title=Election officials’ sample ballot shows how they seek to distinguish two Dan Sullivans in U.S. Senate race|first=Alex|last=DeMarban|date=July 1, 2026|work=[[Anchorage Daily News]]}}</ref>

Daniel James Sullivan and Daniel Scott Sullivan are also unrelated to each other, and unrelated to former [[List of mayors of Anchorage, Alaska|Anchorage mayor]] [[Dan Sullivan (Anchorage mayor)|Daniel Albert Sullivan]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeMarban |first=Alex |title=Namesake challenger to Sen. Dan Sullivan remains defiant despite state investigation |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/06/10/namesake-challenger-to-sen-dan-sullivan-remains-defiant-despite-state-investigation/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=Anchorage Daily News|date=2026-06-10|quote=}}</ref>

=== Campaign ===
Peltola's entry into the race immediately made the race competitive, according to most predictors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kondik |first=Kyle |date=2026-01-13 |title=Alaska Senate Race Comes Onto the Competitive Board with Peltola’s Entry |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/alaska-senate-race-comes-onto-the-competitive-board-with-peltolas-entry/ |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref> She still faces significant hurdles, such as Sullivan's incumbency and lack of a prominent Republican challenger, the unpopularity of the national Democratic Party in Alaska, and a reduction in cross-party support. [[Lisa Murkowski]], Alaska's other U.S. Senator and a noted [[moderate]] Republican, had endorsed Peltola in her [[2022 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|2022]] and [[2024 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|2024]] bids for U.S. House, but she endorsed Sullivan in this race instead.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-12 |title=Former Rep. Mary Peltola jumps into Alaska Senate race |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/12/peltola-alaska-senate-2026-midterms-00721596 |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref> However, as Trump's unpopularity grew, especially amidst the [[2026 Iran war]], Peltola's chances of flipping the Senate seat grew.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beacon |first=Alaska |date=2026-06-18 |title=Alaska among 9 states to decide if Dems flip US Senate |url=https://www.juneauindependent.com/post/alaska-among-9-states-to-decide-if-dems-flip-us-senate |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=Juneau Independent |language=en}}</ref>

Over the course of the primary campaign, a [[super PAC]] called Fair Deal Alaska registered to a [[virtual office]] address in [[Wasilla, Alaska|Wasilla]] spent around $770,000 promoting Green Party candidate [[Richard Grayson (writer)|Richard Grayson]] and Democrat [[Carol Hafner]] in what the ''[[Alaska Beacon]]'' and the ''[[Anchorage Daily News]]'' described as an apparent attempt to dilute support for Peltola in the general election.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite news |last=Samuels |first=Iris |date=August 13, 2026 |title=Millions pour into Alaska to boost fringe U.S. Senate candidates |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/13/millions-pour-into-alaska-to-boost-fringe-us-senate-candidates/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260814003724/https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/13/millions-pour-into-alaska-to-boost-fringe-us-senate-candidates/ |archive-date=August 14, 2026 |access-date=August 13, 2026 |work=[[Anchorage Daily News]]}}</ref> Another PAC called American Democracy Project spent over $240,000 to promote Democrat David Leslie.<ref name=":5" /> A similar group called Right for Alaska spent $1.2 million promoting Republican Gerald Heikes and [[Alaskan Party]] candidate Earl "Skip" Southworth, who were considered more likely to draw support from Dan S. Sullivan.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Herz |first=Nathaniel |date=August 3, 2026 |title=As Alaska’s U.S. Senate campaign heats up, super PACs boost out-of-state candidates |url=https://alaskabeacon.com/2026/08/03/as-alaskas-u-s-senate-campaign-heats-up-super-pacs-boost-out-of-state-candidates/ |work=[[Alaska Beacon]]}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

Both Grayson and Leslie expressed concern about the outside spending on their behalf to the ''Anchorage Daily News''. Grayson—a [[satirical candidate]] living in Arizona—said that he supported Peltola and pledged to withdraw if he advanced to the general election.<ref name=":5" />

== General election ==
===Campaign===
Democratic candidate David Leslie placed fourth in the primary. Leslie, a [[democratic socialism|democratic socialist]] who had criticized Peltola's stances on the [[Gaza genocide]], environmental protection, and actions by [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE), initially said he would not withdraw but later reversed course, citing "pressure from not just the Alaska Democratic leadership, but many different institutions of power".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Herz |first1=Nathaniel |title=This Democratic Socialist could cost Mary Peltola votes in November. But he says he’d actually boost her. |url=https://anchoragepress.com/this-democratic-socialist-could-cost-mary-peltola-votes-in-november-but-he-says-hed-actually-boost-her/ |access-date=September 27, 2026 |work=[[Anchorage Press]] |date=August 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260903140950/https://anchoragepress.com/this-democratic-socialist-could-cost-mary-peltola-votes-in-november-but-he-says-hed-actually-boost-her/ |archive-date=September 3, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="DropsOut">{{cite news |last1=DeMarban |first1=Alex |title=Alaska’s 4th-place U.S. Senate finisher drops out, elevating GOP candidate to ballot |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/09/01/alaskas-4th-place-us-senate-finisher-drops-out-elevating-gop-candidate-to-ballot/ |access-date=September 27, 2026 |work=[[Anchorage Daily News]] |date=September 1, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922113331/https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/09/01/alaskas-4th-place-us-senate-finisher-drops-out-elevating-gop-candidate-to-ballot/ |archive-date=September 22, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Leslie's withdrawal allowed Republican [[perennial candidate]] Gerald Heikes to advance to the general election.<ref name="DropsOut"/>

On September 23, ''[[The New York Times]]'' published allegations from anonymous aides who had worked for Peltola's congressional office and Senate campaign. The report included text messages showing that Peltola had used an ableist slur and expressed hope that a board member of a local [[Planned Parenthood]] chapter "dies of a botched abortion". The anonymous aides also claimed that Peltola had used a homophobic slur, shoved a congressional aide, and ordered congressional aides to feed crickets to her family's pet chameleon. The Peltola campaign claimed that some of the allegations were false or exaggerated, and said that many of the alleged outbursts could be attributed to stress from the death of Peltola's husband and mother while she was serving in Congress.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Browning |first1=Kellen |title=Angry Outbursts, Slurs, and Firings: Tumult Rocks a Key Senate Campaign |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/23/us/politics/mary-peltola-alaska-senate-race.html |access-date=September 27, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=September 23, 2026}}</ref> The [[Alaska Democratic Party]] and Republican Senator [[Lisa Murkowski]] also defended Peltola, while Senator Sullivan and the [[Alaska Republican Party]] condemned her. Alaskan political analysts and operatives interviewed by the ''[[Anchorage Daily News]]'' did not believe the allegations would have a major impact on the election.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kanagy |first1=Mary |title=How ex-staffers’ allegations of hostile behavior by Peltola might affect Alaska’s key U.S. Senate race |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/09/26/how-ex-staffers-allegations-of-hostile-behavior-by-peltola-might-affect-alaskas-key-us-senate-race/ |access-date=September 27, 2026 |work=[[Anchorage Daily News]] |date=September 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260926191309/https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/09/26/how-ex-staffers-allegations-of-hostile-behavior-by-peltola-might-affect-alaskas-key-us-senate-race/ |archive-date=September 26, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>
